title: Why Ohio Stadium Is Called "The House That Harley Built"
description:
Ohio State football is in the news this week, and its home, Ohio Stadium, still carries an old nickname: "The House That Harley Built." Here's how one Columbus high school star, Chic Harley, turned a team that couldn't beat Michigan into the reason for a 66,000-seat concrete horseshoe.
🚶 Visiting San Diego? Explore its history on a guided tour with Fable: https://fablehospitality.com

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

0:00 Ohio Stadium's nickname
0:06 1897: the first game against Michigan
0:12 No wins against Michigan for 20+ years
0:16 1916: Chic Harley joins the team
0:21 Ohio State's first conference title
0:27 Overflow crowds at Ohio Field
0:31 1919: the first win over Michigan, 13-3
0:37 1920: the stadium fund drive
0:43 A horseshoe of poured concrete
0:49 October 1922: the dedication game
0:55 The House That Harley Built today

Note: "Fans hung from trees and walls" follows accounts of overflow crowds at Ohio Field (Spectrum News, Ohio State University Archives). Ohio State had no wins against Michigan from 1897 to 1918 (two ties); the first win was 13-3 in Ann Arbor on October 25, 1919. The 1920 Stadium Campaign raised more than $1 million in pledges; the stadium opened in 1922 with 66,210 seats and was dedicated against Michigan on October 21, 1922 (Michigan 19, Ohio State 0). The nickname credits Harley's popularity for the crowds that made the stadium necessary.

Images (public domain): The Makio, Ohio State University yearbook, 1917, 1920 and 1923 editions (Internet Archive): Ohio Stadium in spring, the stadium skeleton and a 1922 game in the new stadium (1923); Chic Harley portrait, "Why Ohio State Needs a Stadium", "Ohio State's Proposed Stadium" and the 1919 Michigan game play-by-play chart (1920); Chic Harley in uniform, the 1916 champions and an Ohio Field crowd (1917). Score cards drawn in code.
Maps drawn in code from Natural Earth (world-atlas) and US Census (us-atlas) outlines.
Narration voice is synthetic.
